llm_extracted_info.main_contributions: The paper introduces RWKU, a Real-World Knowledge Unlearning benchmark for Large Language Models (LLMs). This benchmark addresses the challenge of erasing sensitive, copyrighted, or harmful knowledge memorized by LLMs. RWKU features a practical 'zero-shot knowledge unlearning' task setting where neither forget nor retain corpora are accessible. It utilizes 200 real-world famous people as unlearning targets, demonstrating their widespread presence in various LLMs. The benchmark provides a comprehensive evaluation framework, including a forget set with four Membership Inference Attack (MIA) methods and nine types of adversarial attack probes to rigorously test unlearning efficacy, and a retain set to assess locality and utility across general ability, reasoning, truthfulness, factuality, and fluency. Experimental findings reveal that models are highly susceptible to adversarial and fill-in-the-blank probes post-unlearning, balancing unlearning efficacy and locality is challenging, batch-target unlearning is significantly harder, and classic gradient ascent, negative preference optimization, and in-context unlearning methods perform relatively well. The benchmark also contributes to research in knowledge probing, localization, and model jailbreak.
llm_extracted_info.methodology: The RWKU benchmark defines a novel 'zero-shot knowledge unlearning' scenario where only the unlearning target (a famous person) and the original model are provided. To enable existing unlearning methods, a synthetic forget corpus (Cs_f) is generated by prompting the original model to create text descriptions related to the unlearning targets. For data collection, 200 famous people were selected from Wikipedia based on popularity (page views), and their memorization in LLMs was quantified using Exact Memorization (EM) and Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL). Probes were constructed using GPT-4 to generate query-answer pairs from Wikipedia passages, filtered by LLaMA3 8B, and then manually verified. Neighbor probes were created from hyperlinks on Wikipedia pages, filtered by popularity and GPT-4. The evaluation framework comprises a 'Forget Assessment' and a 'Retain Assessment'. Forget assessment measures knowledge memorization (fill-in-the-blank probes evaluated with ROUGE-L recall) and knowledge manipulation (question-answer probes and nine types of adversarial attack probes, also with ROUGE-L recall). Membership Inference Attacks (LOSS, Zlib Entropy, Min-K% Prob, Min-K%++ Prob) are used to audit retained knowledge. Retain assessment evaluates locality (neighbor perturbation using fill-in-the-blank and question-answer probes on a neighbor set) and model utility (general ability with MMLU, reasoning ability with Big-Bench-Hard (BBH), truthfulness with TruthfulQA, factuality with TriviaQA, and fluency with AlpacaEval). Six baseline unlearning methods were tested: In-Context Unlearning (ICU), Representation Engineering (RepE), Gradient Ascent (GA), Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), Negative Preference Optimization (NPO), and Rejection Tuning (RT), using full fine-tuning, partial-layer fine-tuning, or LoRA.
llm_extracted_info.experimental_setup: Experiments were conducted on LLaMA3-Instruct (8B) and Phi-3 Mini-4K-Instruct (3.8B), with LLaMA2-Chat (7B) and Mistral-Instruct-v0.2 (7B) also referenced. Unlearning scenarios included single-target (results averaged over 100 unlearning targets) and batch-target unlearning (with target sizes of 10, 20, 30, 40, and 50). The synthetic forget corpus (Cs_f) was generated by prompting the original model, and a pseudo ground-truth forget corpus (C*_f) was derived from Wikipedia descriptions for comparison. Training details involved 3 epochs for methods using the synthetic corpus, 4 epochs for the pseudo ground-truth corpus (GA*), and 2 epochs for batch-target unlearning. Learning rates were selected via grid search (1e-8 to 1e-5), using AdamW optimizer with 20-step warm-up. LoRA fine-tuning used a rank of 8 and an alpha of 16, typically with ten times higher learning rates than full fine-tuning. Experiments utilized eight A100 GPUs. Evaluation metrics for the forget set and neighbor set were ROUGE-L recall. MIA efficacy was primarily reported using LOSS scores. Model utility was assessed using 5-shot accuracy for MMLU, 3-shot EM scores for BBH, 6-shot accuracy for TruthfulQA, 6-shot F1 scores for TriviaQA, and weighted average of bi- and tri-gram entropies for AlpacaEval.
llm_extracted_info.limitations: The primary limitation of RWKU is its reliance on a single knowledge source, specifically real-world famous people, as unlearning targets. This choice was made due to the extensive research and attention factual knowledge about entities has received in fields like knowledge probing and editing. The authors clarify that their main focus is to introduce a novel perspective for LLM knowledge unlearning and provide a comprehensive evaluation framework, rather than to cover all possible knowledge types.
llm_extracted_info.future_research_directions: Future research directions include diversifying knowledge sources beyond famous people to include event knowledge and concept knowledge, as new instances (e.g., 100 real-world historical events) are being collected. The authors also plan to incorporate more advanced attack methods, such as gradient-based attacks, and adopt more comprehensive evaluation metrics that can effectively balance unlearning efficacy and locality. Furthermore, the benchmark is intended to contribute to research areas such as knowledge probing, knowledge localization, and model jailbreak, by enabling further exploration of these related challenges.
